white-collar = relating to office or professional work rather than manual labour
blue-collar = relating to manual or industrial work, often paid by the hour
public sector = the part of the economy run by government, such as schools and hospitals
private sector = businesses owned by individuals or companies, not by the state
third sector = charities, social enterprises and other not-for-profit organisations
government official = a person employed by the state to run public administration
knowledge worker = someone whose main capital is expertise, analysis or design rather than physical labour
manufacturing industry = the sector that makes physical goods in factories
service industry = the sector that provides services rather than goods, such as retail or hospitality
gig economy = work sold in short tasks via apps, with little job security
labour market = the supply of and demand for paid work in an economy
workforce = all the people available for or engaged in work in a place
skilled labour = workers trained in a trade or technical craft
unskilled work = jobs that need little formal training on day one
manual labour = work done mainly with the hands and body
clerical job = office work such as filing, data entry and correspondence
middle management = managers between senior leaders and front-line staff
senior management = the group of directors and heads who set strategy
board of directors = the group legally responsible for governing a company
chief executive = the highest-ranking manager running a company day to day
